== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glascow-14]] is assessed at 55% (possible). Wagstaff Kennedy’s 1817 birth fits Isaac-14’s 1786 Currituck generation and the particular inherited descendant family. The held memorial and FamilySearch material identify Wagstaff’s later life, but his saved biography provides no independent father clause.

=== Original heirship review — 30 October 2026 ===
The existing father [[Glascow-14|Isaac Glasgow]] is now assessed at '''97% confident inference''', superseding the earlier 62% grade. The original 1851 Weakley deed calls its grantors the heirs of deceased Isaac Glasgow and conveys land originally surveyed in his name. The acknowledgment expands the distinctive Wagstaff K. name, agreeing with the existing Weakley family and independently held cemetery context. No birthday discrepancy is silently resolved. Numerous other heirs match Isaac’s existing family, including Elijah, William C., Wagstaff K., John G., Joseph D. and Jesse Glasgow, with the Adams couple. This supports confident fatherhood by the combined specific family group, rather than a generic same-name or age match.<ref name="WeakleyHeirs1851">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSKJ-RS12-5 Weakley County Register of Deeds, pp. 410–411], DGS 008151469, image 213; deed 20 February 1851, acknowledgment 14 March, registered 15 March. Original inspected 30 October 2026.</ref>

The record directly states heirship, not a literal child clause. Husbands are among the grantors and are not treated as biological children. This is a profile-specific confident inference; full middle names, vital dates, mothers and upstream ancestry are not proved by the deed. The acknowledgment expands the distinctive Wagstaff K. name, agreeing with the existing Weakley family and independently held cemetery context. No birthday discrepancy is silently resolved.
